title: Marked mapping complexes are full unions of components
statement:
Use fully scaled categorical patterns and their fibered marked objects from [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], marked simplicial sets, flat and sharp markings and coordinatewise product markings from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and Kan complexes from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha\})$ be a small such pattern, let $W=(W,M)\to\bar C=(C,S)$ be any marked object, and let $Z\to\bar C$ be $\mathfrak P$-fibered. Define
$$K_Z=\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(W^\flat,Z),\qquad \operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(A,Z)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/\bar C}(A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Z).$$
Then $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(W,Z)\hookrightarrow K_Z$ is the full simplicial subset on those vertices $h:W\to Z$ carrying every edge of $M$ to a marked edge of $Z$. This full subset is a union of connected components of the Kan complex $K_Z$: if one vertex in a component preserves the marking, every vertex in that component does, and the subset contains every simplex with vertices in those components. This description is natural for postcomposition by marked maps between fibered objects. The empty domain and components with no marking-preserving vertices are allowed.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484: full simplicial subset description of sharp marked mapping complexes; its union-of-components refinement. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical fact.
